passages.text: VOLCANO, a burning mountain, from the top of which issue fire, smoke, ashes, and streams of melted matter called lava.
The fire of volcanoes is fed by vast beds of sulphur, pyrites, and coal within the earth, which, being moistened by water, ferment and take fire of themselves.
That volcanoes are all near the sea is a proof that the water of the sea, penetrating to these fires, raises the vapours which cause the eruption.
The lava is the earth and stones of the mountain itself, melted by the fire and poured out.
The earthquakes which commonly precede eruptions are caused by the same subterraneous fire endeavouring to find a vent.
When the combustible matter is consumed the volcano is extinguished, and becomes a common mountain.
Such mountains as have burned since the memory of man are few; Etna, Vesuvius, and Hecla being the chief.
A volcano is a rupture in the crust of a planet that allows hot lava, volcanic ash and gases to escape from a magma chamber below the surface.
Magma forms when rock in the mantle or lower crust partly melts, because of falling pressure, added water or added heat.

Most volcanoes occur where tectonic plates pull apart or push together, especially around the Pacific Ocean in the Ring of Fire. Others form over hotspots, such as Hawaii, or in continental rifts far from the sea, such as in East Africa.
Lava is magma that reaches the surface. It rises from deep below the volcano rather than coming from the volcano's own rock.
Water dissolved in magma turns to gas as the magma rises, and this gas drives explosive eruptions.
Rising magma causes swarms of small earthquakes, which are used to forecast eruptions.
A volcano is called extinct when it is not expected to erupt again, usually because it no longer has a supply of magma.
About 1,350 potentially active volcanoes exist on land worldwide, and many more lie on the ocean floor.

reasons: Rare terms appear in both: lava, ashes, eruption, earthquakes before eruptions, extinct volcanoes.
Magma scores well but covers only the molten rock, not the volcano.

alignments.label: A burning mountain

wikipedia.quote: allows hot lava, volcanic ash and gases to escape from a magma chamber

alignments.note: The lava, ash and gas are described correctly. Nothing burns: the heat comes from molten rock.

alignments.label: Burning sulphur and coal

britannica.quote: fed by vast beds of sulphur, pyrites, and coal within the earth

wikipedia.quote: Magma forms when rock in the mantle or lower crust partly melts

alignments.note: There is no underground fire. Rock deep in the earth melts without burning anything.

alignments.label: All near the sea

britannica.quote: That volcanoes are all near the sea

wikipedia.quote: in continental rifts far from the sea, such as in East Africa

alignments.note: Many are near coasts because plate boundaries run there, not because they need the sea.

alignments.label: Vapour drives eruptions

britannica.quote: raises the vapours which cause the eruption

wikipedia.quote: Water dissolved in magma turns to gas as the magma rises, and this gas drives explosive eruptions

alignments.note: Steam does drive eruptions. The water is in the magma, not sea water running onto a fire.

alignments.label: Where lava comes from

britannica.quote: the earth and stones of the mountain itself, melted by the fire

wikipedia.quote: It rises from deep below the volcano rather than coming from the volcano's own rock

alignments.note: The mountain does not melt itself. It is built from lava that came up from below.

alignments.label: Earthquakes before eruptions

britannica.quote: caused by the same subterraneous fire endeavouring to find a vent

wikipedia.quote: Rising magma causes swarms of small earthquakes

alignments.note: Right that they come first and that something below seeks a way out. That something is magma, not fire.

alignments.label: Extinct volcanoes

britannica.quote: When the combustible matter is consumed the volcano is extinguished

wikipedia.quote: usually because it no longer has a supply of magma

alignments.note: Volcanoes do die when their supply runs out. The supply is magma, not fuel.

alignments.label: Only a few are active

britannica.quote: Such mountains as have burned since the memory of man are few

wikipedia.quote: About 1,350 potentially active volcanoes exist on land worldwide

alignments.note: The 1797 count is limited to the volcanoes Europeans knew: Etna, Vesuvius and Hecla.

suggestedQuestions: What did the 1797 entry think made volcanoes hot?
Was the 1797 entry right that volcanoes are all near the sea?
Which 1797 claims about volcanoes still hold?

What did the 1797 entry think made volca.answer: Underground beds of sulphur, pyrites and coal that took fire when moistened [B2]. Wikipedia says there is no fire: magma forms when rock in the mantle or lower crust partly melts [W2], and lava rises from deep below rather than from the mountain's own rock [W4].

Was the 1797 entry right that volcanoes.answer: No. It took their position as proof that sea water reaches the fires [B3]. Wikipedia says most volcanoes lie along tectonic plate boundaries, many around the Pacific, but some form far from the sea, for example in East Africa [W3].

Which 1797 claims about volcanoes still.answer: Only observations, not explanations. Earthquakes do come before eruptions [B5] [W6], steam does drive eruptions [B3] [W5], and volcanoes do become extinct [B6] [W7]. In each case the 1797 entry gives the wrong reason: a fire under the ground [B2], where Wikipedia has magma [W2].
